key_insight: A linear dual-field finite element scheme reproduces cross-helicity balance and preserves exact Alfvénic alignment in unforced ideal incompressible MHD when either Elsässer energy is initially zero.
engineering_relevance: Preserving alignment and conservation laws supports physically consistent simulations of conducting-fluid flows in periodic domains.
method: Reassign the two magnetic-field approximations to integer and half-integer time levels.
Redesign Lorentz and induction couplings within linear staggered updates.
Link energy and cross-helicity balances to a nonnegative Elsässer-energy representation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments illustrate aligned-state preservation in ideal MHD and alignment dynamics under weak dissipation; the abstract reports no quantitative accuracy or runtime results.
watch_item: The formulation targets periodic domains, so applicability to engineering boundary conditions requires further assessment.
paper_title: A linear dual-field finite element method for incompressible MHD, part I: cross-helicity and Alfvénic alignment in periodic domains
